issues.main_description_html:
UI reference: #185 — Update editor toolbar layout structure

Implement the editor toolbar layout described in the UI task above. Specification below is copied from #185.

brainstorming.md - Update Toolbar Editor Layout

branch: product-docs
file: docs\superpowers\specs\2026-07-06-editor-layout-structure-brainstorming.md
Sources: User brief, current editor topbar, current editor 2D/3D workspace, current floating toolbar behavior
Audience: Product, UI/UX, QA, and Claude UI UX Pro Max

RESULT

branch: UI-UX-Update-editor-toolbar-layout

1. Shared Understanding

Goal

Make editor mode easier to understand by separating 2D drawing tools from shared viewer controls, while keeping the current editor behavior, visual style, and compact workspace feel.

Product Intent

The editor should feel like a professional indoor mapping workspace. Users should always understand which tools affect the 2D floor plan, which controls affect the 3D viewer, and which controls apply to both. The change is mostly about layout clarity, grouping, and discoverability, not a new editor concept.

Main User Problem

The current toolbar mixes file actions, drawing tools, visibility settings, panel controls, and camera controls in one long row. This makes the workspace feel busy and can make users unsure whether a control affects the 2D panel, the 3D panel, or the whole editor.

Desired Outcome

Users should be able to answer three questions at a glance:

  • Where do I go for file-level actions?
  • Which tools do I use to draw or edit the 2D floor plan?
  • Which controls do I use to view, inspect, and adjust the 2D/3D workspace?

2. Current Layout Observations

The current editor already has useful building blocks:

  • A compact top navbar with MapThru branding, a File dropdown, save state, theme toggle, Share, Preview, and Save.
  • A 2D plan panel and a 3D view panel that can appear together or separately.
  • A floating bottom toolbar with drawing tools, undo/redo, zoom, camera, object visibility, image visibility, and panel toggles.
  • Existing visual styling with small icon buttons, rounded controls, soft borders, editor color tokens, and floating tool surfaces.
  • An Add Level flow that already owns floor and floor plan upload behavior.
  • Export-related behavior that can be grouped into one Export area instead of multiple visible toolbar buttons.

The layout does not need a full redesign. It needs stronger organization and clearer tool ownership.

3. Product Intent

Editor mode should feel calm, direct, and work-focused. The user is building a Digital Twin from a Floor Plan, so the interface should support precise work without making the control surface feel crowded.

The improved layout should:

  • Keep the existing editor identity.
  • Make 2D editing tools feel attached to the 2D plan panel.
  • Make 3D and shared viewer controls feel separate from drawing tools.
  • Keep repeated actions quick to reach.
  • Reduce disabled or duplicate controls.
  • Avoid changing the user's mental model of saving, previewing, drawing, and switching panels.

4. In Scope

  • File dropdown content and labels.
  • Bottom toolbar organization.
  • Separation between 2D-only drawing tools and shared viewer controls.
  • Placement of the Shapes dropdown inside the 2D toolbar.
  • Object visibility grouping.
  • Floor plan image visibility and opacity behavior.
  • Panel display mode naming and placement.
  • Guidance for keeping the current editor visual style.
  • Non-technical interaction guidance for UI UX Pro Max.
  • Acceptance criteria and QA scenarios for layout clarity.

5. Out of Scope

  • Rebuilding the editor engine.
  • Changing drawing behavior.
  • Defining shape creation behavior beyond toolbar placement and menu grouping.
  • Changing how walls, curves, windows, areas, points, or safety annotations are stored.
  • Changing save, autosave, preview, share, or project persistence behavior.
  • Changing Add Level behavior beyond recognizing it as the home for floor plan loading.
  • Creating a new visual design system.
  • Adding new third-party dependencies.
  • Creating backend endpoints.
  • Implementing the layout in code as part of this brainstorming document.

6. Recommended Layout Direction

Recommended Approach: Keep the Editor Shell, Split Tool Ownership

Keep the current editor shell and visual language, but reorganize actions into three clear zones:

  1. File and project actions in the top navbar File dropdown.
  2. 2D drawing tools near or inside the 2D plan workspace.
  3. Shared viewer controls in a separate compact control group for navigation, visibility, image overlay, and panel mode.

This approach is recommended because it improves clarity without changing the product too much. Users keep the same editor surface, but the controls become easier to scan and understand.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative A: Keep one long toolbar

This preserves the current structure, but it keeps mixing drawing, viewing, file, and panel actions. It does not solve the main confusion.

Alternative B: Create a full left-side professional tool dock

This could work for a larger editor redesign, but it is too large for this task. It may also change the style and behavior more than needed.

Alternative C: Move every control into top menus

This would make the canvas cleaner, but drawing tools would become slower to reach. Editor mode needs direct tool access.

7. File Dropdown Changes

Purpose

The File dropdown should contain clear project-level navigation and help actions. It should not show disabled placeholders or actions that have moved elsewhere.

Recommended Items

Menu item Destination / behavior User meaning
Dashboard Redirects to /dashboard Leave editor and return to the project workspace.
New File Redirects to /start Start a new project or new file flow.
Help Redirects to /help Open help content for the editor.

Remove From File Dropdown

  • Disabled New File placeholder, if it does not navigate.
  • Disabled Export placeholder, if export is handled by a real Export control.
  • About, unless there is a clear product requirement for it.
  • Add Floor, unless Product wants File to remain the entry point for level management.

Navigation Notes

  • Dashboard should keep the existing unsaved-change protection.
  • New File should also protect unsaved changes before leaving the editor.
  • Help may open in the same app route or a separate help surface, but the user should not lose work unexpectedly.

Suggested Copy

  • File
  • Dashboard
  • New File
  • Help
  • Unsaved changes
  • Leave without saving
  • Cancel

8. Toolbar Cleanup

Purpose

The visible editor toolbar should stop carrying file import/export actions that belong elsewhere. This keeps the main toolbar focused on active editing and viewing.

Remove From Visible Toolbar

  • Load Floorplan.
  • Save Editable TXT.
  • Export GeoJSON.

Where These Actions Belong

Current action New home Reason
Load Floorplan Add Level Loading a floor plan is part of adding or managing a level.
Save Editable TXT Export It is an output action, not a drawing tool.
Export GeoJSON Export It is an output action, not a drawing tool.

Export Group

Export should become the clear home for downloadable outputs. It can include:

  • Editable TXT.
  • GeoJSON.
  • Future export formats, if needed.

The Export group can live in the topbar or as a compact button near shared viewer controls, but it should not be mixed into the drawing tool strip.

9. Tool Grouping Strategy

Group A: 2D Drawing Tools

These tools belong to the 2D floor plan editing workflow:

  • Wall.
  • Curve.
  • Window.
  • Area.
  • Shapes.
  • Point.
  • Safety Annotation.
  • Undo.
  • Redo.

The 2D drawing tools should visually belong to the 2D panel. They should feel like tools for shaping Map Geometry and adding indoor map annotations.

Shapes Dropdown

Shapes should appear as one grouped dropdown inside the 2D drawing tools, not as three separate top-level toolbar buttons.

Recommended dropdown items:

  • Rectangle.
  • Circle.
  • Polygon.

Place Shapes near Area, Point, and Safety because it belongs to the same 2D floor plan editing surface. Shapes should remain a layout-level grouping in this document; the detailed creation behavior stays in 2026-07-06-editor-shapes-tools-brainstorming.md.

Recommended 2D tool order:

  1. Wall.
  2. Curve.
  3. Window.
  4. Area.
  5. Shapes.
  6. Point.
  7. Safety.
  8. Undo.
  9. Redo.

Group B: Shared Viewer Controls

These controls support viewing, inspecting, and managing the workspace:

  • Zoom In.
  • Zoom Out.
  • Fit Plan.
  • Reset 3D Camera.
  • Object visibility.
  • Snap to Grid.
  • Floor Plan Image visibility.
  • Floor Plan Image opacity.
  • Panel display mode.

These controls are not drawing tools. They should be grouped separately so users do not confuse viewing controls with content creation tools.

Group C: Context Selection Tools

Selection-specific actions can remain contextual:

  • Door/window size.
  • Door swing.
  • Room height.
  • Area type.
  • Wall thickness.
  • Delete selected.
  • Deselect.

These should appear only when relevant and should not crowd the default toolbar.

10. 2D Panel Behavior

Purpose

The 2D panel is where users draw and edit the Floor Plan. The drawing toolbar should follow the 2D panel so the relationship is obvious.

Recommended Behavior

  • When 2D and 3D are both visible, the 2D drawing tools should sit closer to the 2D panel than the 3D panel.
  • When 2D only is active, the 2D drawing tools should remain visible and centered within the 2D workspace.
  • When 3D only is active, 2D drawing tools should hide or become clearly unavailable.
  • The current active drawing tool should remain visually obvious.
  • The Shapes dropdown should show an active state when Rectangle, Circle, or Polygon is selected.
  • Undo and Redo should stay with the 2D drawing group because they affect drawing and editing changes.

User-Friendly Guidance

Use spatial placement to explain tool ownership. If a tool creates or edits 2D geometry, place it where the user is looking while editing 2D geometry.

Suggested 2D Tool Labels

  • Wall
  • Curve
  • Window
  • Area
  • Shapes
  • Point
  • Safety
  • Undo
  • Redo

11. 3D / Shared Viewer Behavior

Purpose

The 3D viewer needs camera and display controls, but it should not compete with the 2D drawing workflow.

Recommended Behavior

  • Keep Zoom In, Zoom Out, and Fit Plan in a shared viewer group.
  • Keep Reset 3D Camera in the shared viewer group, but make its 3D meaning clear.
  • If 3D only is active, prioritize the Reset 3D Camera control.
  • If 2D only is active, Reset 3D Camera can remain available but should be visually quieter or disabled if it does not apply.
  • Shared viewer controls should remain near the active workspace and should not be mistaken for drawing tools.

Suggested Viewer Labels

  • Zoom in
  • Zoom out
  • Fit plan
  • Reset 3D camera
  • View options

12. Panel Mode Behavior

Purpose

Panel mode should be understandable as a display choice, not two unrelated toggle buttons.

Recommended Display Modes

Use a single panel mode control with three options:

Option Meaning
2D only Show only the 2D floor plan editor.
3D only Show only the 3D viewer.
2D & 3D Show both panels side by side.

Recommended Behavior

  • Always keep at least one panel visible.
  • Make the active panel mode visually selected.
  • When switching to 2D only, center the 2D drawing tools in the available 2D workspace.
  • When switching to 3D only, hide or reduce 2D drawing tools and emphasize viewer controls.
  • When switching to 2D & 3D, keep the layout balanced and place 2D tools near the 2D side.

Suggested Copy

  • Panel
  • 2D only
  • 3D only
  • 2D & 3D

13. Visibility and Export Grouping

Object Visibility

Replace the generic Show Icons idea with clear object-specific visibility controls.

Recommended object visibility dropdown:

  • Show doors.
  • Show windows.
  • Show shapes.
  • Show points.
  • Show safety annotations.
  • Show room labels.

This makes the control easier to understand because users can choose exactly what appears in the workspace.

Floor Plan Image

The Floor Plan Image control should include:

  • A visibility toggle.
  • An opacity slider only when the image is visible and an image exists.

Do not show the opacity slider when it cannot affect anything.

Snap to Grid

Snap to Grid should stay near viewer or editing assist controls. It should feel like an editing aid, not an object type.

Export

Export should collect output actions in one place:

  • Export editable TXT.
  • Export GeoJSON.

The visible toolbar should show one Export entry at most, not separate export buttons.

14. User Flows

Flow A: Return to Dashboard

  1. User opens File.
  2. User selects Dashboard.
  3. If there are unsaved changes, the editor asks for confirmation.
  4. User confirms or cancels.
  5. User returns to /dashboard.

Flow B: Start a New File

  1. User opens File.
  2. User selects New File.
  3. If there are unsaved changes, the editor asks for confirmation.
  4. User confirms or cancels.
  5. User moves to /start.

Flow C: Draw in 2D

  1. User views the 2D panel.
  2. User sees drawing tools close to the 2D workspace.
  3. User selects Wall, Curve, Window, Area, Point, or Safety.
  4. The active tool state is visible.
  5. User can Undo or Redo from the same 2D tool group.

Flow C2: Choose a Shape Tool

  1. User views the 2D panel.
  2. User opens Shapes from the 2D drawing toolbar.
  3. User sees Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon grouped together.
  4. User selects one shape type.
  5. The Shapes control shows an active state while the selected shape tool is active.
  6. User still understands that shape behavior is part of the 2D editing workflow, not a 3D viewer control.

Flow D: Inspect in 3D

  1. User switches to 3D only or keeps 2D & 3D.
  2. User sees viewer controls separately from drawing tools.
  3. User uses Reset 3D Camera or zoom controls without scanning through drawing actions.

Flow E: Change Visible Objects

  1. User opens Object Visibility.
  2. User toggles doors, windows, shapes, points, safety annotations, or room labels.
  3. The workspace updates while keeping the dropdown state clear.

Flow F: Adjust Floor Plan Image

  1. User opens image visibility controls.
  2. User turns the Floor Plan Image on.
  3. The opacity slider appears.
  4. User adjusts opacity.
  5. If the image is turned off, the opacity slider is hidden.

Flow G: Switch Panel Mode

  1. User opens Panel control.
  2. User chooses 2D only, 3D only, or 2D & 3D.
  3. Panels update.
  4. Tool placement updates so controls still feel attached to the correct workspace.

15. Accessibility and Usability Notes

  • Icon-only buttons need clear accessible names and tooltips.
  • Controls should have at least a comfortable clickable area.
  • The active tool should be indicated by more than color alone.
  • Dropdown items should be keyboard reachable.
  • The Shapes dropdown should be keyboard reachable and should expose Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon as clear menu items.
  • Panel mode should announce the selected state.
  • Disabled controls should explain why they are unavailable where possible.
  • Toolbar groups should not overlap selection toolbars.
  • Long tool labels should collapse gracefully into icons with tooltips.
  • The layout should avoid horizontal overflow on smaller editor widths.
  • The UI should remain clear in light and dark editor themes.

16. Suggested UI Copy

File Menu

  • File
  • Dashboard
  • New File
  • Help

2D Drawing Tools

  • Wall
  • Curve
  • Window
  • Area
  • Shapes
  • Rectangle
  • Circle
  • Polygon
  • Point
  • Safety
  • Undo
  • Redo

Viewer Controls

  • Zoom in
  • Zoom out
  • Fit plan
  • Reset 3D camera
  • Snap to grid

Visibility

  • Object visibility
  • Show doors
  • Show windows
  • Show shapes
  • Show points
  • Show safety annotations
  • Show room labels

Floor Plan Image

  • Floor plan image
  • Show image
  • Image opacity

Panel Mode

  • Panel
  • 2D only
  • 3D only
  • 2D & 3D

Export

  • Export
  • Editable TXT
  • GeoJSON

17. Acceptance Criteria

File Dropdown

  • File dropdown shows Dashboard, New File, and Help.
  • Dashboard routes to /dashboard.
  • New File routes to /start.
  • Help routes to /help.
  • Disabled placeholder items are removed or avoided.
  • Leaving the editor through Dashboard or New File respects unsaved-change protection.

Toolbar Cleanup

  • Load Floorplan is not shown as a main toolbar button.
  • Save Editable TXT is not shown as a main toolbar button.
  • Export GeoJSON is not shown as a main toolbar button.
  • Load Floorplan is treated as part of Add Level.
  • Editable TXT and GeoJSON are grouped under Export.

Tool Grouping

  • 2D drawing tools are visually separate from viewer controls.
  • Wall, Curve, Window, Area, Shapes, Point, Safety Annotation, Undo, and Redo are grouped as 2D tools.
  • Shapes appears as one dropdown inside the 2D drawing tools.
  • Shapes contains Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon.
  • Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon do not appear as separate top-level toolbar buttons.
  • Selecting a Shapes menu item makes the Shapes control visibly active.
  • Zoom, Fit Plan, Reset 3D Camera, visibility, Snap to Grid, Floor Plan Image, and panel controls are grouped as viewer or workspace controls.
  • The active drawing tool remains clear.

Panel Behavior

  • 2D only mode shows the 2D workspace and keeps 2D drawing tools available.
  • 3D only mode shows the 3D workspace and does not present 2D drawing tools as primary controls.
  • 2D & 3D mode shows both panels and keeps tool ownership visually clear.
  • Users cannot hide both panels at the same time.

Visibility

  • Object visibility uses clear object names.
  • Doors, windows, shapes, points, safety annotations, and room labels can be understood separately.
  • Generic Show Icons is replaced by specific visibility choices.
  • Floor Plan Image opacity appears only when it can be used.

Style

  • The editor keeps its current compact toolbar style.
  • Existing rounded controls, borders, shadows, and editor tokens are preserved.
  • The change does not introduce a marketing-style layout or unrelated visual system.

18. QA Scenarios

  1. User opens File and sees Dashboard, New File, and Help.
  2. User selects Dashboard with no unsaved changes and reaches the dashboard.
  3. User selects Dashboard with unsaved changes and sees a confirmation.
  4. User selects New File and reaches the start flow after any required confirmation.
  5. User can find Help from the File dropdown.
  6. User does not see disabled placeholder File menu items.
  7. User does not see Load Floorplan in the main toolbar.
  8. User can understand that floor plan loading belongs to Add Level.
  9. User does not see separate Save Editable TXT and Export GeoJSON toolbar buttons.
  10. User finds Editable TXT and GeoJSON under Export.
  11. User sees drawing tools grouped separately from viewer controls.
  12. User sees Shapes as a dropdown inside the 2D drawing tools.
  13. User opens Shapes and sees Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon.
  14. User selects Rectangle, Circle, or Polygon and sees Shapes become active.
  15. User does not see Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon as separate top-level toolbar buttons.
  16. User switches to 2D only and can still use drawing tools.
  17. User switches to 3D only and drawing tools are hidden or visually de-emphasized.
  18. User switches to 2D & 3D and can understand which tools belong to 2D.
  19. User toggles doors without also toggling all icons.
  20. User toggles windows without also toggling all icons.
  21. User toggles shapes separately from points and safety annotations.
  22. User toggles points and safety annotations separately.
  23. User toggles room labels separately.
  24. User turns on the Floor Plan Image and sees the opacity slider.
  25. User turns off the Floor Plan Image and the opacity slider no longer distracts.
  26. Keyboard-only user can reach File, drawing tools, Shapes, viewer controls, and panel mode.
  27. Toolbar groups do not overlap contextual selection toolbars.

19. Open Questions

Question Recommended default Owner
Should Help open /help in the same tab or a new tab? Same tab, with unsaved-change protection if leaving editor state. Product / Design
Should Add Level remain accessible from the File menu? Prefer no; keep File focused on navigation and help unless Product wants level management there. Product
Where should the Export entry live? Prefer the topbar near Save/Preview or a compact shared-control menu, not inside the 2D drawing tools. Design
Where should Shapes sit in the 2D tool order? Place it after Area and before Point so it reads as object geometry, not annotation. Design
Should 2D drawing tools hide completely in 3D only mode? Yes, hide them or clearly de-emphasize them so users do not try to draw in 3D. Product / Design
Should Reset 3D Camera be disabled in 2D only mode? Prefer disabled or visually quiet if the 3D panel is hidden. Design / Engineering
Should object visibility affect both 2D and 3D views or only the active panel? Prefer both views for consistency unless a panel-specific need is defined later. Product
Should Show shapes live in Object Visibility from v1? Yes, include it so shape visibility is managed with other object visibility controls. Product / Design

20. Risks

Risk Impact Mitigation
Toolbar becomes too fragmented. Users may need to look in too many places. Keep only three zones: File, 2D tools, shared viewer controls.
2D tools are hidden too aggressively. Users may think editing is unavailable. Hide 2D tools only in 3D only mode; show them clearly in 2D modes.
Export becomes hard to find. Users may miss downloadable outputs. Use a clear Export label and place it near top-level editor actions.
Visibility dropdown becomes too long. Users may avoid it. Keep only object-level visibility choices that users understand.
Shapes crowds the 2D toolbar. The toolbar may feel harder to scan. Use one Shapes dropdown instead of separate Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon buttons.
Shapes is mistaken for Area. Users may confuse room boundaries with room objects. Place Shapes near Area, but keep it as a clearly named dropdown with object-focused menu items.
The design drifts away from the current editor style. The editor feels inconsistent. Reuse current compact floating controls, icons, borders, shadows, and editor tokens.
Panel switching causes confusion. Users may lose track of tool ownership. Make panel mode explicit and move/de-emphasize tools based on visible panels.

21. Design Summary for UI UX Pro Max

The editor layout should remain visually conservative and workspace-focused. Keep the current MapThru editor shell, compact topbar, floating control surfaces, rounded icon buttons, soft borders, subtle shadows, and editor color tokens.

The main design improvement is clearer tool ownership:

  • File actions belong in the File dropdown.
  • 2D drawing tools belong with the 2D plan panel.
  • Shapes belongs as a dropdown inside the 2D drawing tools, with Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon grouped inside it.
  • Shared viewer controls belong in their own workspace control group.
  • Export actions belong under Export.
  • Visibility choices should name the actual objects users can show or hide, including shapes.
  • Panel mode should be one clear control with 2D only, 3D only, and 2D & 3D options.

This should make editor mode feel less crowded without changing the core editing workflow. The user should feel that the interface is guiding them: draw in 2D, inspect in 3D, control visibility from one place, and manage files from the top navigation.

RESULT

Editor toolbar reorganized (branch feature/207-editor-toolbar-layout, commit b260f8a).

Done

  • File menu wired: Dashboard -> /dashboard, New File -> /start, Help -> /help (all through the unsaved-changes guard). Disabled Export/About/New File placeholders and redundant Add Floor removed (Add Level still reachable from the level panel).
  • File I/O (Load editable TXT, Save editable TXT, Export GeoJSON) grouped into one Export popover; no longer separate buttons in the drawing strip.
  • Object visibility (doors, windows, shapes, markers, room labels) grouped into a single menu; generic "Show icons" renamed to "Show markers". Snap-to-grid kept as a standalone editing aid.
  • Added a /help placeholder page so the File -> Help link is not a 404.

Already satisfied in existing code (untouched)

  • Shapes is already a grouped dropdown.
  • Floor-plan image opacity slider only shows when the image is visible.
  • Panel toggles already guard against hiding both 2D and 3D at once.

Deliberate deviations (need product sign-off)

  • Load editable TXT placed in the Export popover, not Add Level: it imports engine geometry (.txt), whereas Add Level uploads an image and runs an AI scan — different flows.
  • Points and safety share one "Show markers" toggle: the engine only exposes a combined icons visibility flag; per-type split needs engine work.
  • Panel mode kept as two guarded toggles instead of a single 2D-only / 3D-only / 2D&3D segmented control: the functional requirement (cannot hide both) is met; the single-control restyle was skipped as cosmetic.

Verification

  • tsc --noEmit and ESLint clean.
  • Not yet driven in a live editor session (needs an active project + session); all handlers are reused as-is, only relocated into popovers.

issues.main_description_html:
Implement linked Information object label types

Source

  • Brainstorming source: docs/superpowers/brainstorming/2026-07-09-linked-information-object-label-types-brainstorming.md

Summary

Add object label style controls for objects that have linked Information. Each linked object label should support one selected display type: text only, Font Awesome icon only, logo image only, or photo image only.

The default should be text only. Visual-only labels should stay compact on the map and reveal the linked Information text on hover or click.

User Story

As an editor, I want to choose how each linked object label appears on the map, so I can make the map clearer using text, icons, logos, or photos depending on what best represents the place.

Required Behavior

Label Type Choices

Each linked Information object label must support these display types:

  • Text only
  • Icon only
  • Logo image only
  • Photo image only

Text only is the default.

Text Only

Text only should:

  • Show the linked Information name or title.
  • Show a small colored dot.
  • Use no filled background.
  • Avoid large pill or card styling.
  • Stay readable on both vector and satellite maps.

If the title is long, keep the visible label compact and allow the full name to appear on hover or click.

Icon Only

Icon only should:

  • Use a Font Awesome icon selected from a dropdown.
  • Show the icon without permanent text on the map.
  • Reveal the linked Information name or title on hover or click.
  • Fall back gracefully if no icon has been selected.

Logo Image Only

Logo image only should:

  • Show only the Information logo image on the map.
  • Not show permanent text beside the logo.
  • Reveal the linked Information name or title on hover or click.
  • Fall back gracefully if the Information has no logo.

Photo Image Only

Photo image only should:

  • Let the user choose one uploaded Information photo from a dropdown.
  • Show a thumbnail preview in the photo selection dropdown.
  • Show only the selected photo image on the map.
  • Not show permanent text beside the photo.
  • Reveal the linked Information name or title on hover or click.
  • Fall back gracefully if the selected photo is missing or deleted.

Hover And Click

For icon, logo, and photo labels:

  • Hover reveals the linked Information name or title.
  • Click keeps the name or title visible while the label is selected.
  • Moving away hides hover text unless the label is selected.
  • The marker should not jump, resize awkwardly, or move the map layout.

For text labels:

  • Text is already visible.
  • Hover or click may reveal a fuller title if the visible label is shortened.

Zoom Behavior

When the map is zoomed far out:

  • Show a small colored dot.
  • Do not show text.
  • Do not show full logo, photo, or icon details.
  • Keep the map easy to scan.

When the map is zoomed close in:

  • Show the selected label type.
  • Text labels show text and dot.
  • Icon labels show the selected icon.
  • Logo labels show the logo image.
  • Photo labels show the selected photo image.

Dot Color

The small dot should use a color that matches the label type or object type.

Suggested direction:

  • Text label: calm neutral or project accent color.
  • Icon label: icon category color.
  • Logo label: brand or image label color.
  • Photo label: photo label color.

The dot must remain readable on both vector and satellite maps.

Map Style Adaptation

Labels should adapt automatically when the user switches between vector and satellite map styles.

On vector maps:

  • Labels can be quieter.
  • Text can use normal contrast.
  • Dots can use clean solid colors.
  • Shadows should be subtle.

On satellite maps:

  • Labels need stronger contrast.
  • Text may need an outline, shadow, or stronger contrast treatment.
  • Dots may need a light or dark ring.
  • Images may need a subtle edge so they remain visible over photo backgrounds.

Users should not need to manually adjust label colors after switching map style.

Label Selection UI

The linked Information area should include a clear control for label style.

Suggested label:

Object label style

Choices:

  • Text only
  • Icon only
  • Logo image only
  • Photo image only

When Icon only is selected, show an icon dropdown.

When Logo image only is selected, show the current Information logo and a friendly missing-logo state if there is no logo.

When Photo image only is selected, show a photo dropdown with thumbnail previews from the Information photos.

Empty And Missing Data States

  • If text only is selected but the Information title is missing, use a friendly fallback such as Information.
  • If icon only is selected but no icon has been chosen, ask the user to choose an icon or fall back to text only until an icon is selected.
  • If logo image only is selected but the Information has no logo, show a friendly editor message and fall back to text only on the map.
  • If photo image only is selected but there are no uploaded photos, show a friendly editor message and fall back to text only on the map.
  • If a selected photo is deleted later, fall back gracefully and ask the user to choose another photo.

Accessibility

  • Every label should have a readable name for assistive technology.
  • Hover-only text should also be available by keyboard focus.
  • Icon, logo, and photo labels should still provide the Information title when focused, hovered, or selected.
  • Far-zoom dots should have readable names and should not rely only on color.

Non-Goals

  • Do not redesign the full Information editor.
  • Do not redesign the full map toolbar.
  • Do not change how users create Information records.
  • Do not change how users upload logos or photos, except for selecting which existing photo appears as the label.
  • Do not add a custom label builder.
  • Do not change unlinked marker behavior except where it needs to remain visually consistent.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Linked Information labels can be set to text only, icon only, logo image only, or photo image only.
  • Text only is the default.
  • Text only appears as clean text plus a small dot, without a filled background.
  • Icon only uses a Font Awesome icon selected from a dropdown.
  • Logo image only displays only the logo image on the map.
  • Photo image only displays only the selected Information photo on the map.
  • Photo selection uses uploaded Information photos and shows thumbnail previews.
  • Logo and photo labels do not show permanent text on the map.
  • Icon, logo, and photo labels reveal the Information text on hover and click.
  • Far zoom shows small colored dots instead of full labels.
  • Close zoom shows the selected label type.
  • Labels stay readable on both vector and satellite maps.
  • Missing icons, logos, or photos fall back gracefully and guide the user to fix the choice.
  • Label hover and keyboard focus reveal the same identifying information.

Verification

  • Add or update focused tests where practical for label type selection, fallback behavior, and zoom/map-style display rules.
  • Manually verify text, icon, logo, and photo label types.
  • Manually verify vector and satellite readability.
  • Manually verify far zoom dot behavior and close zoom full label behavior.
  • Run lint/typecheck/test commands required by the repo before marking complete.

RESULT

Linked Information object label types implemented (branch feature/208-linked-info-label-types, commit 70f59f6).

Done

  • Data model: labelType (text | icon | logo | photo), labelIcon, labelPhoto added to the Information record. Stored once per record, so every object linking it renders alike (per-object override can be added later if needed).
  • Selection UI: "Object label style" control on the InformationModal Media tab — style picker, Font Awesome icon grid, photo picker with thumbnails, and friendly missing-logo/photo states. Default is text.
  • Rendering: resolveLabelRender() applies the chosen type and falls back to text when the icon/logo/photo asset is missing. Icon/logo/photo labels reveal the title on hover, focus, or while selected.
  • Zoom: far zoom collapses every marker to a bare colored dot; close zoom shows the full label (DOT_ZOOM calibration knob in MapObjectMarkers).
  • Map style: satellite gets stronger contrast (rings + white text-shadow) so labels stay readable over imagery.
  • All visible form controls in InformationModal converted to shadcn (Input, Textarea, Select); only the two hidden file-input triggers stay native.
  • Added the three @FortAwesome packages (fontawesome-svg-core, free-solid-svg-icons, react-fontawesome).
  • Replaced the now-unused pickLinkedVariant + its test with resolveLabelRender unit tests covering the fallback matrix.

Decision

  • labelType stored per Information record (not per object). A shared Information linked by multiple objects renders the same on all of them.

Notes

  • Font Awesome uses default autoAddCss (runtime CSS injection) — a brief flash of oversized icons is possible on first paint; functionally correct.

Verification

  • tsc --noEmit, ESLint (0 errors), 16 unit tests, and pnpm build all pass.
  • Not driven in a live editor session (needs an active project with a linked Information object).

UI reference: #205 — Create 360 pano viewer modal

Implement the 360 pano viewer modal described in the UI task above. Specification below is copied from #205.

Implement linked Information 360 pano modal

RESULT

Brach : UIUX-update-editor-tour-key

Source

  • Brainstorming source: docs/superpowers/brainstorming/2026-07-09-linked-information-pano-modal-brainstorming.md

Summary

Update the linked Information area so pano content is easy to find and view. When a selected map object is linked to an Information record that has pano content, show a clear View 360 Pano button. Clicking the button should open an in-app modal that displays the 360 degree pano while keeping the user in the same map context.

User Story

As a GoThru 3D Floormap user, I want to open a linked 360 pano from the Information area, so I can review the pano without leaving the editor or preview experience.

Required Behavior

Linked Information Area

When the selected linked Information has pano content:

  • Show a View 360 Pano button in the linked Information area.
  • Place the button near the top of the Information layout, close to the Information title and secondary label.
  • Keep the button visible before long descriptions, photos, contact details, or extra links.
  • Do not change the linked Information when the user clicks the button.

When the selected linked Information does not have pano content:

  • Do not show the View 360 Pano button.
  • Keep the normal linked Information layout clean and unchanged.

Recommended linked Information order:

  1. Logo or small visual, if available.
  2. Information title.
  3. Information name or object type.
  4. View 360 Pano button, if pano content exists.
  5. Direction or navigation action, if available.
  6. Description.
  7. Photos.
  8. Hours, phone, website, links, and tags.

View 360 Pano Button

Suggested button label:

View 360 Pano

Suggested icon:

  • Use a 360, orbit, panorama, or similar viewing icon.

Button behavior:

  • Opens the pano modal.
  • Keeps the selected map object selected.
  • Does not navigate away from the editor or preview page.
  • Does not change the linked Information.
  • Is easy to tap on mobile.
  • Is easy to identify in a compact panel.

Pano Modal

The modal must display the selected 360 degree pano in a focused overlay.

Required modal content:

  • Modal title based on the Information title or selected object name.
  • Close button.
  • 360 degree pano viewer area.
  • Loading state while the pano loads.
  • Fallback action to open the pano externally if the embedded viewer cannot load.

Suggested modal copy:

  • Loading: Loading 360 pano...
  • Error: This pano could not load here.
  • Fallback action: Open in TourMkr
  • Close button label: Close pano
  • Viewer title: 360 pano for the Information title

The pano viewer should be the main content of the modal. Avoid surrounding it with extra panels or heavy explanation.

Modal Behavior

When the user clicks View 360 Pano:

  • The modal opens above the current map.
  • The background map remains visible but inactive.
  • The selected Information remains the same behind the modal.
  • Focus moves into the modal.

When the user closes the modal:

  • The modal disappears.
  • The user returns to the same linked Information area.
  • The same map object remains selected.
  • Focus returns to the View 360 Pano button when possible.

Close options:

  • Close icon button.
  • Escape key.
  • Optional backdrop click, if this matches the product modal pattern.

Required States

  • No linked Information
  • Linked Information without pano
  • Linked Information with pano
  • Pano button visible
  • Pano button hidden
  • Opening modal
  • Modal loading
  • Modal loaded
  • Modal error
  • Modal closed

Error And Recovery

  • If the linked Information has no pano content, do not show the button.
  • If the pano cannot display inside the modal, keep the modal open and show This pano could not load here.
  • Show Open in TourMkr as the recovery action when embedded display fails.
  • Show Loading 360 pano... instead of leaving a blank viewer area during slow loading.
  • The modal must always be closable.

Accessibility

  • View 360 Pano must be a real button.
  • The button must have clear accessible text.
  • The modal must have a clear title.
  • The modal must announce itself as a dialog.
  • Focus must move into the modal when it opens.
  • Focus should return to the pano button when the modal closes.
  • Escape must close the modal.
  • The close button must have a clear label.
  • Loading and error states must be readable by screen readers.
  • The selected map object must not be lost when the modal closes.

Non-Goals

  • Do not redesign the full editor.
  • Do not redesign the full Information creation flow.
  • Do not change how users select a pano for an Information record.
  • Do not show the pano button when no pano exists.
  • Do not support multiple pano modals at the same time.
  • Do not add unrelated dashboard, account, or publishing actions.
  • Do not replace the map or selected object with a pano-only page.
  • Do not require the user to leave the editor or preview experience.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A linked Information record with pano content shows a View 360 Pano button.
  • A linked Information record without pano content does not show the button.
  • The button appears near the top of the linked Information area.
  • Clicking the button opens an in-app modal.
  • The modal displays the 360 degree pano.
  • The modal has a clear title.
  • The modal has a visible close button.
  • The modal can be closed with Escape.
  • Closing the modal returns the user to the same selected map object and linked Information.
  • The map does not navigate away when opening the pano.
  • A loading state appears while the pano loads.
  • A fallback action appears if the pano cannot load inside the modal.
  • The layout works in narrow panels and small screens.
  • The pano viewing experience feels connected to the linked Information area.

Verification

  • Add or update focused tests where practical for the linked Information pano button and modal behavior.
  • Verify linked Information without pano does not show the button.
  • Verify linked Information with pano opens the modal.
  • Verify modal close behavior preserves map selection context.
  • Run lint/typecheck/test commands required by the repo before marking complete.

RESULT (implementation)

Note: the ## RESULT section above belongs to the UI reference task #205 (branch UIUX-update-editor-tour-key) and was carried over when the spec was copied. This section is the implementation result for #209.

Sub task :

Implement preview page publish navbar

  • publish

Source

  • Brainstorming source: docs/superpowers/brainstorming/2026-07-09-preview-page-navbar-brainstorming.md

Summary

Add an editor-like navbar to the preview page, with preview-specific publishing controls. The navbar should show MapThru branding, draft/published status, light/dark theme toggle, publish/unpublish controls, public sharing, and a live project link.

The preview navbar must feel related to the editor navbar, but it must not include editor-only actions such as save, file menu, collaboration sharing, add floor, or preview.

User Story

As a project owner reviewing a preview, I want to see whether the project is draft or published and manage publishing from the preview page, so I can publish, share, unpublish, or open the public project without returning to editing mode.

Required Behavior

Navbar

Add a top navbar to the preview page.

The navbar must include:

  • MapThru branding with logo.
  • Project status label: Draft or Published.
  • Light/dark theme toggle.
  • Publish button when the project is still a draft.
  • Share button when the project is published.
  • Unpublish button when the project is published.
  • View project live button when the project is published.

The publish and unpublish actions must be primary actions.

Draft State

When the project is not published, show:

  • MapThru branding with logo.
  • Draft status label.
  • Light/dark theme toggle.
  • Primary Publish button.

Do not show:

  • Share
  • Unpublish
  • View project live

Published State

When the project is published, show:

  • MapThru branding with logo.
  • Published status label.
  • Light/dark theme toggle.
  • Share button.
  • Primary Unpublish button.
  • View project live button.

Publish Confirmation

Clicking Publish must open a friendly confirmation modal before publishing.

Suggested copy:

  • Title: Publish project?
  • Helper: This will make your project available to everyone with the public link. You can unpublish it later.
  • Confirm button: Publish project
  • Cancel button: Cancel

Behavior:

  • Start publishing only after the user confirms.
  • If the user cancels, keep the project in draft state.
  • On success, update the status label to Published.
  • On success, replace draft actions with published actions.

Suggested feedback:

  • Loading: Publishing...
  • Success: Project published
  • Error: Project could not be published. Try again.

Unpublish Confirmation

Clicking Unpublish must open a friendly confirmation modal before unpublishing.

Suggested copy:

  • Title: Unpublish project?
  • Helper: People with the public link will no longer be able to view this project. You can publish it again when you are ready.
  • Confirm button: Unpublish project
  • Cancel button: Cancel

Behavior:

  • Start unpublishing only after the user confirms.
  • If the user cancels, keep the project in published state.
  • On success, update the status label to Draft.
  • On success, replace published actions with draft actions.
  • Unpublishing removes public access but does not delete the project.

Suggested feedback:

  • Loading: Unpublishing...
  • Success: Project unpublished
  • Error: Project could not be unpublished. Try again.

Share Button

The preview Share button must mean public distribution, not editor collaboration.

Requirements:

  • Show it only when the project is published.
  • Use copy that clearly says public link and embed code.
  • Do not include people, members, invites, permissions, or collaboration language.

Suggested accessible label or tooltip:

Share published project

Share Modal

Clicking Share opens a share modal inspired by Google Maps sharing behavior.

The modal must include:

  • Copy shareable link.
  • Copy embed code.

Share link section:

  • Section label: Share link
  • Helper text: Anyone with this link can view the published project.
  • Button: Copy link
  • Success feedback: Link copied

Embed section:

  • Section label: Embed map
  • Helper text: Use this code to embed the published project on a website.
  • Button: Copy embed code
  • Success feedback: Embed code copied

View Project Live

The View project live button appears only in published state.

Behavior:

  • Opens the published public project in a new browser tab.
  • Does not change preview page state.
  • Does not close the preview page.

Suggested accessible label:

Open published project in a new tab

Theme Toggle

The preview navbar must include a light/dark theme toggle that matches the editor navbar style.

Requirements:

  • User can switch between light and dark mode.
  • Preview page updates visually.
  • Selected mode is clear.
  • Control is keyboard accessible.

Required States

  • Loading publish status
  • Draft
  • Publish confirmation open
  • Publishing
  • Published
  • Unpublish confirmation open
  • Unpublishing
  • Publish error
  • Unpublish error
  • Share modal open
  • Copy link success
  • Copy embed code success
  • Copy error

Accessibility

  • Navbar should be a clear top navigation landmark.
  • Status should be readable as text.
  • Theme toggle should have an accessible label.
  • Publish and unpublish buttons should be keyboard reachable.
  • Publish confirmation should clearly explain that everyone with the public link can access the project.
  • Unpublish confirmation should clearly explain that everyone with the public link will lose access.
  • Share modal should have a clear title.
  • Share modal should trap focus while open.
  • Escape should close the share modal.
  • Copy buttons should announce success feedback.
  • View project live should communicate that it opens a new tab.
  • Loading and error states should not rely on color alone.

Non-Goals

  • Do not redesign the preview map itself.
  • Do not add editor drawing tools to preview.
  • Do not add the editor file menu to preview.
  • Do not add save controls to preview.
  • Do not make the preview Share button a collaboration invite feature.
  • Do not add member permissions to the share modal.
  • Do not redesign the public live project page.
  • Do not change how the editor navbar works.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The preview page has a navbar that visually resembles the editor navbar.
  • The navbar shows MapThru branding with logo.
  • The navbar shows Draft when the project is not published.
  • Draft state shows a primary Publish button.
  • Clicking Publish opens a confirmation modal before publishing.
  • The publish confirmation explains that everyone with the public link can access the project.
  • The user can cancel publishing and remain in draft state.
  • Draft state does not show Share, Unpublish, or View project live.
  • The navbar shows Published when the project is published.
  • Published state shows Share, primary Unpublish, and View project live.
  • Clicking Unpublish opens a confirmation modal before unpublishing.
  • The unpublish confirmation explains that people will no longer be able to access the public project.
  • The user can cancel unpublishing and remain in published state.
  • Share opens a modal for public sharing, not collaboration.
  • The share modal includes Copy link.
  • The share modal includes Copy embed code.
  • Copy actions show success feedback.
  • View project live opens the live project in a new tab.
  • Publish and unpublish states update the navbar labels and actions.
  • Light/dark theme toggle is available.
  • The layout works on desktop and mobile.

Verification

  • Add or update focused tests where practical for preview navbar states and modal behavior.
  • Verify draft state, publish confirmation, published state, unpublish confirmation, share modal, and copy actions manually.
  • Run lint/typecheck/test commands required by the repo before marking complete.

issues.main_description_html:
UI reference: #206 — Create preview page publish navbar
Brainstorming source: docs/superpowers/brainstorming/2026-07-09-preview-page-navbar-brainstorming.md

Implement Implement Publish/ Unpublish Project at Dashboard Layout per the shared Preview Page Publish Navbar spec below.

Preview Page Navbar Brainstorming

Feature name: Preview Page Publish Navbar
Product: GoThru 3D Floormap / MapThru
Generated: 2026-07-09
Audience: Product, design, and Claude UI UX Pro Max
Tone: Non-technical
Scope: Preview page navbar, draft/published status, theme toggle, publish/unpublish actions, share modal, and live project link
Branch: product-docs

1. Purpose

The preview page should feel connected to the editor, but it should not feel like editing mode.

Add a navbar to the preview page that resembles the editor navbar visually, while showing only the actions that make sense for preview and publishing.

The preview navbar should help users answer:

  • Am I looking at a draft or a published project?
  • Can I publish this project?
  • Can I unpublish this project?
  • Can I share this published project?
  • Can I open the public live project?
  • Can I switch light and dark mode?

2. Product Context

The editor page already has a navbar with MapThru branding, theme mode, share, preview, and save actions.

The preview page currently focuses on showing the map experience. That is useful, but users also need a lightweight publishing control surface when reviewing the project before release.

The preview navbar should borrow the editor navbar's structure and polish, but it should not copy editor-only actions. Preview is for review, publishing, and sharing, not for collaboration editing.

3. Main Change

Add a top navbar to the preview page.

The navbar should include:

  • MapThru branding with logo.
  • Project status label: Draft or Published.
  • Light/dark theme toggle.
  • Publish button when the project is still a draft.
  • Share button when the project is published.
  • Unpublish button when the project is published.
  • View project live button when the project is published.

The publish and unpublish actions should be primary actions.

Both publish and unpublish should ask for confirmation before changing the project status.

Publishing confirmation should explain that the project will become available to everyone with the public link.

Unpublishing confirmation should explain that people will no longer be able to access the public project.

4. User Mindset

Project Owner

This user is reviewing the project before sharing it. They need to know whether the project is still a draft and where to publish it.

Publisher

This user has already published the project and now needs share tools, embed code, the live public link, or an unpublish option.

Reviewer

This user may be checking the preview experience before sending it to a client. They need the navbar to stay helpful without making the page feel like an editor workspace.

5. Recommended Direction

Recommended Approach: Editor-Like Navbar, Preview-Specific Actions

Use the editor navbar as the visual reference:

  • Same MapThru brand placement.
  • Same compact topbar height and spacing.
  • Same light/dark toggle style.
  • Same restrained professional tone.

But change the right-side actions to match preview status.

Draft state:

  • Status label: Draft
  • Theme toggle
  • Primary Publish button

Published state:

  • Status label: Published
  • Theme toggle

  • Can I publish this project?
  • Can I unpublish this project?
  • Can I share this published project?
  • Can I open the public live project?
  • Can I switch light and dark mode?

2. Product Context

The preview navbar should borrow the editor navbar's structure and polish, but it should not copy editor-only actions. Preview is for review, publishing, and sharing, not for collaboration editing.

3. Main Change

The navbar should include:

  • MapThru branding with logo.
  • Project status label: Draft or Published.
  • Light/dark theme toggle.
  • Publish button when the project is still a draft.
  • Share button when the project is published.
  • Unpublish button when the project is published.
  • View project live button when the project is published.

The publish and unpublish actions should be primary actions.

Both publish and unpublish should ask for confirmation before changing the project status.

Publishing confirmation should explain that the project will become available to everyone with the public link.

Unpublishing confirmation should explain that people will no longer be able to access the public project.

4. User Mindset

This user is reviewing the project before sharing it. They need to know whether the project is still a draft and where to publish it.

Publisher

This user has already published the project and now needs share tools, embed code, the live public link, or an unpublish option.

This user may be checking the preview experience before sending it to a client. They need the navbar to stay helpful without making the page feel like an editor workspace.

Recommended Approach: Editor-Like Navbar, Preview-Specific Actions

  • Same MapThru brand placement.
  • Same compact topbar height and spacing.
  • Same light/dark toggle style.
  • Same restrained professional tone.

But change the right-side actions to match preview status.

Draft state:

  • Status label: Draft
  • Theme toggle
  • Primary Publish button

Published state:

  • Status label: Published
  • Theme toggle
  • Share button
  • Primary Unpublish button
  • View project live button

This approach keeps the product familiar while making preview mode clearly different from editor mode.

This keeps the page visually clean, but users have no obvious publishing controls or status feedback.

Option B: Copy The Full Editor Navbar

This would be familiar, but it would bring editor-only actions into preview mode. The preview Share button could be confused with editor collaboration sharing.

This keeps visual consistency while showing only status, theme, publishing, sharing, and live-view actions.

Left Zone

Show:

  • MapThru logo.
  • MapThru brand name.
  • Status label near the brand or project context.

Suggested status labels:

  • Draft
  • Published

The status label should be visible text, not color alone.

Right Zone

Show actions based on project status.

Draft state:

  • Theme toggle.
  • Publish button.

Published state:

  • Theme toggle.
  • Share button.
  • Unpublish button.
  • View project live button.

The navbar should not include editor-only buttons such as save, file menu, collaboration share, add floor, or preview.

When the project is not published, the navbar is focused on publishing.

Required elements:

  • MapThru branding with logo.
  • Draft status label.
  • Light/dark theme toggle.
  • Primary Publish button.

Suggested copy:

  • Status: Draft
  • Primary action: Publish

Do not show:

  • Share
  • Unpublish
  • View project live

Reason:

Sharing and live viewing only make sense after the project is published.

When the project is published, the navbar changes to sharing and publishing management.

Required elements:

  • MapThru branding with logo.
  • Published status label.
  • Light/dark theme toggle.
  • Share button.
  • Primary Unpublish button.
  • View project live button.

  • Status: Published

  • Primary action: Unpublish
  • Live action: View project live

The preview Share button must not look or feel like the editor share button used for collaboration.

In preview published mode, share means public distribution.

Share this published project

Suggested button label:

Share

Suggested accessible label or tooltip:

Share published project

Purpose:

Give the user a public URL they can send to someone.

Suggested confirm button:

Publish project

Suggested cancel button:

Cancel

Suggested loading copy:

Publishing...

Suggested success feedback:

Project published

Project could not be published. Try again.

Unpublishing...

Project unpublished

Project could not be unpublished. Try again.

Unpublish project?

Suggested confirmation helper:

People with the public link will no longer be able to view this project. You can publish it again when you are ready.

Suggested confirm button:

Unpublish project

Suggested cancel button:

Cancel

The confirmation should be clear and calm. The user should understand that unpublishing removes public access, but it does not delete the project.

The View project live button appears only in published state.

Button behavior:

  • Opens the published public project in a new browser tab.
  • Does not change preview page state.
  • Does not close the preview page.

Suggested button label:

View project live

Suggested accessible label:

Open published project in a new tab

This button should feel like a secondary action, not the primary action.

The preview navbar should include a light/dark theme toggle.

The toggle should match the editor navbar's theme toggle style so users recognize it.

Required behavior:

  • User can switch between light and dark mode.
  • The preview page updates visually.
  • The selected mode should be clear.
  • The control should be keyboard accessible.

Suggested labels:

  • Light mode
  • Dark mode

Do not make the theme toggle compete with publish or unpublish.

16. Required States

Loading Status

The preview page is still loading project publish state.

Suggested status label:

Loading

Actions should be disabled or hidden until the state is known.

Draft

Show:

  • Draft
  • Theme toggle
  • Publish

Publishing

Show:

  • Draft
  • Theme toggle
  • Disabled Publishing... button

Publish Confirmation Open

The user clicked Publish, and the confirmation modal is open.

Suggested title:

Publish project?

Suggested helper:

This will make your project available to everyone with the public link. You can unpublish it later.

Actions:

  • Cancel
  • Publish project

Published

Show:

  • Published
  • Theme toggle
  • Share
  • Unpublish
  • View project live

Unpublishing

Show:

  • Published
  • Theme toggle
  • Disabled Unpublishing... button
  • Keep other actions stable or disabled according to product behavior.

Unpublish Confirmation Open

The user clicked Unpublish, and the confirmation modal is open.

Suggested title:

Unpublish project?

Suggested helper:

People with the public link will no longer be able to view this project. You can publish it again when you are ready.

Actions:

  • Cancel
  • Unpublish project

Show a recoverable message:

Project could not be published. Try again.

Unpublish Error

Show a recoverable message:

Project could not be unpublished. Try again.

The share modal is open above the preview page.

After copy link or copy embed code succeeds, show short success feedback.

  • Same MapThru brand treatment.
  • Same border and background rhythm.
  • Same light/dark toggle style.
  • Clear status pill or label.

  • Save button.
  • Editor collaboration share language.
  • Member invitation UI.
  • Crowded toolbars.
  • Large marketing-style banners.

  3. Share and live-view actions when published.

1. Purpose

The preview page should feel connected to the editor, but it should not feel like editing mode.

Add a navbar to the preview page that resembles the editor navbar visually, while showing only the actions that make sense for preview and publishing.

  • Can I open the public live project?
  • Can I switch light and dark mode?

2. Product Context

The editor page already has a navbar with MapThru branding, theme mode, share, preview, and save actions.

The preview page currently focuses on showing the map experience. That is useful, but users also need a lightweight publishing control surface when reviewing the project before release.

The preview navbar should borrow the editor navbar's structure and polish, but it should not copy editor-only actions. Preview is for review, publishing, and sharing, not for collaboration editing.

3. Main Change

Add a top navbar to the preview page.

The navbar should include:

  • MapThru branding with logo.
  • Project status label: Draft or Published.
  • Light/dark theme toggle.
  • Publish button when the project is still a draft.
  • Share button when the project is published.
  • Unpublish button when the project is published.
  • View project live button when the project is published.

The publish and unpublish actions should be primary actions.

Both publish and unpublish should ask for confirmation before changing the project status.

Publishing confirmation should explain that the project will become available to everyone with the public link.

Unpublishing confirmation should explain that people will no longer be able to access the public project.

4. User Mindset

This user is reviewing the project before sharing it. They need to know whether the project is still a draft and where to publish it.

Publisher

This user has already published the project and now needs share tools, embed code, the live public link, or an unpublish option.

This user may be checking the preview experience before sending it to a client. They need the navbar to stay helpful without making the page feel like an editor workspace.
